title: Mesóclise and Highly Formal Pronoun Placement
summary: Understand mesóclise forms such as far-se-á and when they appear in formal Brazilian writing.

sections.heading: What mesóclise is
sections.body: **Mesóclise** places an object pronoun inside a future or conditional verb form: **far-se-á**, **dir-se-ia**. It is rare in speech and mostly appears in legal, ceremonial, or very formal writing.

examples.en: One would say that everyone agreed.

examples.pt: Realizar-se-á a cerimônia às dez horas.
examples.en: The ceremony will be held at ten o'clock.

sections.heading: When mesóclise is blocked
sections.body: If a word that attracts the pronoun comes before the verb—such as **não**, **que**, **se**, **talvez**, or many adverbs—use próclise instead of mesóclise.

examples.en: Justice will not be done this way.

examples.pt: Espero que se realize a cerimônia.
examples.en: I hope the ceremony is held.

examples.pt: Talvez se diria outra coisa em público.
examples.en: Perhaps something else would be said in public.

sections.heading: Brazilian practical usage
sections.body: In Brazil, mesóclise can sound solemn, archaic, bureaucratic, or humorous if used outside formal contexts. Most modern communication uses a simpler structure.

examples.pt: A cerimônia será realizada às dez.
examples.en: The ceremony will be held at ten.
I shall send you the documents.

keyPoints: Mesóclise inserts pronouns into future or conditional verb forms.
It is rare in Brazilian speech and marked in writing.
Negative words and many subordinators trigger próclise instead.
Prefer clearer modern alternatives unless analyzing formal texts.

commonMistakes.note: Não attracts the pronoun before the verb.
Mesóclise uses the future form, not the infinitive.
Do not combine ir + infinitive with a mesoclitic future form.
